newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian crops badly hit by drought, frost - farmers.
newsitem.headline: Italian crops badly hit by drought, frost - farmers.

text.p: Unseasonal weather conditions, with drought in northern Italy, rain in the south and frost throughout the country, have caused serious damage to crops, the Italian national farmers' federation Coldiretti said.
In a report specially compiled for Reuters based on regional data so far available, Coldiretti said Italian agriculture had suffered damage put at over two trillion lire ($1.2 billion).
It noted that the inclement conditions this spring, following particularly mild weather at the end of winter, were still continuing.

Coldiretti president Paolo Micolmi has called on the government to take urgent measures, including declaring a state of emergency in at least three regions -- Piedmont, Lombardy and Veneto -- because of the serious threat to agricultural employment, particularly in the fruit and vegetable sector.
Following are region-by-region Coldiretti reports:

PIEDMONT - Because of drought and frost all spring sowings are late, particularly cereals (maize, sunflower and soya), but wheat, barley and sugarbeet are also affected. In the Cuneo area temperatures of as low as four to five degrees below zero have been recorded. Most of the kiwi harvest has been lost and that of peaches and nectarines is only at 50 percent. Widespread damage to production of apples, pears, apricots and plums.

Rice production has been hit by water shortage put at over 50 percent. In viticulture, early varieties of grape affected, with possibility of considerable reduction in production. Colidiretti has asked government to declare a state of emergency.

LOMBARDY - Preliminary estimate of overall damage in region put at over 700 billion lire. Cumulative water shortage since start of 1997 on average equal to 150 mm, which on a regional level corresponds to a deficit of around 3.5 billion cubic metres, a huge amount considering average annual rainfall in Lombardy is around 22 billion cubic metres. All cereal and fodder production in crisis with resulting impact on livestock industry due to high costs breeders will have to pay for animal foodstuffs. Government asked to declare state of emergency.
FRIULI VENEZIA GIULIA - Due to drought and high winds there has been damage to beet crops due to lack of root moisture. Spring sowings are late and vines and orchards have been hit.

VENETO - Due to drought and late frosts, cereal sowings are down 30 percent, beet sowings down 30 percent, fodder sowings down 20 percent and open air vegetable sowings down 40 percent. Government asked to declare state of emergency.
TRENTINO ALTO ADIGE - Drought and frosts have jeopardised 80 percent of fruit production in Italy's main apple-producing region.

EMILIA ROMAGNA - Damage estimated at above 600 billion lire. Romagna in particular hit by frosts with temperatures down to seven degrees below zero. Kiwi production 100 percent lost. Production halved for pears, peaches, plums and kakis. High costs seen for treatment of orchards which has to be carried out even though fruit crop lost.
TUSCANY - Serious damage due to drought and frosts, put at over 500 billion lire, with impact on production of kiwi, tomatoes, potatoes, fresh flowers and vines.
UMBRIA - Frost damage to orchards, vegetables and vines.
CAMPANIA - Frost damage to fruit and vegetable crops put at 300 billion lire.
PUGLIA - Production of olives, cereals and fruit down 10-20 percent due to frost damage.
BASILICATA - Frosts and rain have heavily jeopardised production of cereals, fruit and vegetables.
CALABRIA - Situation serious due to frosts and rain. Damage to production of citrus fruit, fruit and vegetables and olives estimated at over 100 billion lire.
